People connect their own Discord accounts.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Discord account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [discord.com](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
- **Settings:** `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Built in:** nothing to add, only the client to set

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/discord/callback
```

An app that runs the sign-in itself (rather than through the Gateway) also needs its own callback:

```text
https://<app>.<your app domain>/integrations/social/discord
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`. `pnpm everyapp provider show discord` prints the exact URI.

### Make the OAuth app

1. Open [discord.com](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Discord) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set DISCORD_CLIENT_ID DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  discord: { access: "read", why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show discord` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Discord**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `pnpm everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
